name: Semaglutide
used_for: FDA-labeled for chronic weight management and reducing cardiovascular risk in adults with obesity or overweight (Wegovy), MASH with liver fibrosis (Wegovy, accelerated approval), and type 2 diabetes glycemic control, cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction (Ozempic), each alongside diet and activity changes where specified.

entries.text: Wegovy injection: labeled starting dose 0.25 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 4 weeks, with stepwise increases every 4 weeks (0.5 mg, 1 mg, 1.7 mg) toward a maintenance dose that varies by indication (labeled maintenance typically 1.7 to 2.4 mg weekly; label also describes up to 7.2 mg weekly for weight reduction).
entries.population: Adults (and pediatric patients 12 years and older for weight reduction) per the Wegovy label

entries.text: Wegovy tablets: labeled starting dose 1.5 mg orally once daily for 30 days, then 4 mg, then 9 mg in 30-day steps, with a maintenance dose of 25 mg daily.
entries.population: Adults with obesity or overweight per the Wegovy label

entries.text: Ozempic injection: labeled starting dose 0.25 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg weekly, with optional increases to 1 mg and then 2 mg weekly (maximum) after at least 4 weeks at each dose.
entries.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes per the Ozempic label

internet_entries.text: A health information website that carries affiliate links to telehealth providers says people who microdose semaglutide commonly start at 0.05 mg to 0.125 mg once weekly, and that many stay below 0.5 mg weekly. The page notes there is no agreed definition of a microdose and describes the practice as not studied in a protocol.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

internet_entries.text: A prescription discount service blog says some people report using semaglutide microdoses starting as low as 0.05 mg once weekly, and that some take 10 to 100 times lower doses than standard prescriptions. The page presents this as an unstudied off-label practice.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: The Wegovy label states the injection is given once weekly on the same day each week, at any time of day, with or without meals, subcutaneously in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Wegovy label states that if a weekly injection is missed and the next scheduled dose is more than 2 days away, it is given as soon as possible, and if the next dose is less than 2 days away the missed dose is skipped and the regular day is resumed. After 2 or more consecutive missed doses, the label states dose escalation is restarted at a lower dosage to reduce gastrointestinal reactions.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Wegovy label states the tablet form is taken once daily in the morning on an empty stomach with water (up to 4 ounces), swallowed whole, with at least 30 minutes before eating, drinking other beverages, or taking other oral medicines. A missed tablet dose is skipped and the next dose taken the following day.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Wegovy label states an unused pen or syringe is stored in a refrigerator (2 to 8 C) and protected from light, and may be kept at 8 to 30 C for up to 28 days before the cap is removed. A multi-dose FlexTouch pen can be kept for 56 days after first use at 15 to 30 C or in the refrigerator, with the cap on and a new needle used for each injection. The product must not be frozen.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Ozempic label states the weekly dose is given at any time of day with or without meals, and that a missed dose can be administered within 5 days of the missed dose. It states to use a different injection site each week within the same body region, and to inject separately from insulin without mixing.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Ozempic label states a pen is refrigerated (2 to 8 C) before first use, kept in the original carton, and after first use can be stored for 56 days at 15 to 30 C or in the refrigerator, not frozen.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Ozempic label states the day of weekly administration can be changed if necessary, as long as the time between two doses is at least 2 days (more than 48 hours). It also states pens must never be shared between patients, even if the needle is changed, and that when used with insulin the products can be injected in the same body region but not adjacent to each other.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: A telehealth company's blog says the best injection time is whatever can be kept consistent each week, that morning injections may let nausea pass during waking hours while evening injections may suit those who want any nausea overnight, and that a low-fat, low-fiber meal may reduce early nausea.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: A Healthline article on nausea with Ozempic describes eating smaller portions, choosing bland foods, avoiding greasy or spicy foods, taking frequent sips of water, and waiting at least 30 minutes after the injection before trying certain foods such as ginger or mints.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: In the Wegovy label's pooled weight-management trials, gastrointestinal reactions were the most frequent: nausea 44% vs 16% with placebo, diarrhea 30% vs 16%, vomiting 24% vs 6%, constipation 24% vs 11%, and abdominal pain 20% vs 10%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Wegovy label also lists headache (14% vs 10%), fatigue (11% vs 5%), dyspepsia, dizziness, and hair loss among adverse reactions, and hypoglycemia (6% vs 2%) in participants with type 2 diabetes.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Wegovy and Ozempic labels carry a boxed warning of thyroid C-cell tumors: semaglutide caused such tumors in rodents, the relevance to humans is unknown, and the drug is contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Wegovy label lists warnings for acute pancreatitis and acute gallbladder disease, and notes that substantial or rapid weight loss can increase gallbladder risk.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In the Ozempic label's placebo-controlled trials in type 2 diabetes, documented symptomatic hypoglycemia occurred more often with insulin or a sulfonylurea added (for example 29.8% with basal insulin added vs 15.2% with placebo).
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: WebMD patient reviews of Wegovy describe large weight losses for many people (some report tens of pounds over months), alongside frequent nausea, vomiting and constipation; some stop over side effects or cost.
UCLA Health says rapid GLP-1 weight loss can cause a hollowed, older-looking face ('Ozempic face') and contribute to muscle loss, and suggests protein and slower weight loss to limit this.
Cedars-Sinai says 'microdosing' GLP-1s is a social media trend promoted for weight loss and health benefits, but argues there is no evidence that low, intermittent doses work.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Wegovy (semaglutide) injection and tablets, revised June 2026.
research.finding: Lists approved uses for weight reduction, cardiovascular risk reduction, and MASH, with a dose-escalation schedule.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Ozempic (semaglutide) injection.
research.finding: Lists approved uses in adults with type 2 diabetes: glycemic control, cardiovascular risk reduction, and kidney outcomes, with escalation up to 2 mg weekly.

research.summary: STEP 1: randomized, double-blind trial of semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly versus placebo for 68 weeks in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes (Wilding et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: Average weight change was -14.9% with semaglutide versus -2.4% with placebo; nausea and diarrhea were the most common side effects.

research.summary: SUSTAIN-6: randomized trial of once-weekly semaglutide versus placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk (Marso et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: Major cardiovascular events occurred in 6.6% with semaglutide versus 8.9% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.74); retinopathy complications were more frequent with semaglutide.
